newsitem.title: UK: Sumitomo employees out of touch with copper probe.
newsitem.headline: Sumitomo employees out of touch with copper probe.

text.p: Sumitomo Corp is imposing strict intra-company information control on its massive copper trading losses, and is not informing its own traders of how an internal investigation is proceeding, trade sources said.
"No information on the internal inquiry is available within the company. It seems the Sumitomo management does not trust its own employees," a Japanese source close to Sumitomo said.

The Japanese trade house announced on September 19 that its estimated losses from unauthorised copper trading by former star trader Yasuo Hamanaka had risen to $2.60 billion from its initial estimate in June of $1.80.
The sources said Sumitomo president Kenji Miyahara and a vice president are the only people who are fully informed on how the internal inquiry is proceeding.
"The reality is that even Sumitomo traders have quite limited knowledge (about the inquiry) and are seeking information from other firms," another source said.
The trade house fired Hamanaka on June 14, and set up an internal task force to investigate how he built up the massive losses in the world copper market.
